chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from some of our companions from Abd al-Hamid al-Ta'i said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Do I marry the woman and consummate the marriage with her without giving her anything?' He said, 'Yes, it becomes a debt upon you.'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'If he consummates the marriage with her before giving her anything, he has missed the Sunnah, and the dowry is in his liability, and it becomes obligatory upon him to deliver it to her whenever she demands it. And we have clarified that the Sunnah is to give part of the dowry or the entire dowry first. As for that which indicates that if he does not give her the dowry, it is in his liability, it is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: “And give the women [upon marriage] their dowry as a free gift.” And if he specifies a dowry for her, it becomes obligatory upon him to fulfill it according to the apparent meaning of the Quran. And that which indicates this is also what he narrated:'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to marry and consummate without paying the dowry immediately?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while immediate payment is not a condition for the validity of consummation, the mahr becomes a binding debt (dayn) upon the husband. Shaykh al-Tusi elaborates that deferring payment deviates from the Sunnah of promptness, citing the Quranic imperative to give mahr as a 'gift' (nihlah), thereby establishing the unpaid amount as an enforceable liability payable upon the wife's demand.
